Third, it is a unit of account: it gives everything a price tag so you can compare values quickly.

concept_body_en:

The same Rp 50,000 buys more in some places and less in others because prices differ. A high nominal salary does not always mean a rich life if rent, food, and transport are expensive.

Nilai berarti seberapa berguna atau diinginkan sesuatu bagimu. Daya beli berarti seberapa banyak yang bisa kamu beli dengan jumlah uang tertentu. Rp 50.000 yang sama bisa membeli lebih banyak di beberapa tempat dan lebih sedikit di tempat lain karena harganya berbeda. Gaji nominal tinggi tidak selalu berarti hidup kaya jika sewa, makanan, dan transportasi mahal.

title_en: Inflation: Why Your Rupiah Buys Less Over Time
title_id: Inflasi: Mengapa Rupiahmu Membeli Lebih Sedikit dari Waktu ke Waktu
summary_en: Inflation is the slow rise in prices that quietly shrinks the buying power of your cash.
summary_id: Inflasi adalah kenaikan harga yang perlahan-lahan memangkas daya beli uang tunaimu.
concept_body_en:
Inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services over time. When inflation happens, each rupiah buys less than before. Bank Indonesia aims to keep inflation low and stable, around 2.5% plus or minus 1% per year. Low inflation is normal in a growing economy, but high inflation hurts people who keep large amounts of cash.

Inflation does not mean every price rises by the same amount, but the overall cost of living tends to go up. Cash sitting under a pillow loses purchasing powe
concept_body_id:
Inflasi adalah kenaikan harga barang dan jasa secara umum seiring waktu. Ketika inflasi terjadi, setiap rupiah membeli lebih sedikit dari sebelumnya. Bank Indonesia menargetkan inflasi rendah dan stabil, sekitar 2,5% plus minus 1% per tahun. Inflasi rendah adalah hal normal dalam ekonomi yang tumbuh, tetapi inflasi tinggi merugikan orang yang menyimpan uang tunai dalam jumlah besar.

Inflasi tidak berarti setiap harga naik dalam jumlah yang sama, tetapi biaya hidup secara keseluruhan cenderung n
indonesian_example_en: In 2020, Rina could buy a bowl of mie ayam for Rp 12,000. In 2025, the same bowl costs Rp 16,000. She kept Rp 120,000 under her pillow for five years. In 2020 that money bought ten bowls, but in 2025 it buys only seven bowls and leaves some change. Her rupiah amount stayed the same, but her purchasing power fell.

summary_en: Income is money coming in; wealth is what you keep and grow over time.
concept_body_en:
Income is the flow of money you receive, such as salary, allowance, or freelance payments. Wealth is the stock of money and valuable things you already own, minus what you owe. A person can earn a high income but have low wealth if they spend almost everything. Another person can earn less but have more wealth if they save and invest consistently.

Income measures speed; wealth measures the size of your financial reservoir. Long-term financial health depends more on what you keep than on what yo
indonesian_example_en: Andi works as a sales promoter and earns Rp 8,000,000 per month. He rents an expensive apartment, eats out daily, and has zero savings. Budi works as a barista and earns Rp 4,000,000 per month. He lives simply and has saved Rp 15,000,000 in a separate tabungan. Budi has less income but more wealth because he keeps more of what he earns.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Covering needs first makes wants more enjoyable and less stressful.
concept_body_en:
A need is something you must have to live, study, or work safely. Examples include food, shelter, transport, and basic phone credit. A want is something you would like to have but can live without, such as a new outfit, a concert ticket, or a premium streaming subscription.

The line between need and want is not always clear. For example, a basic phone is a need for online classes, but the latest flagship phone is a want. The goal is not to eliminate wants. The goal is to cover needs first, save
indonesian_example_en: Sari gets Rp 1,500,000 monthly allowance. She pays kos Rp 700,000, buys a campus meal card for Rp 400,000, and tops up pulsa for Rp 100,000. Those are needs. She also wants a new pair of sneakers for Rp 600,000 and a streaming subscription for Rp 100,000. If she buys the sneakers first, she may not have enough for kos. If she covers needs and saves Rp 100,000 first, she can plan for the sneakers next month.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: An asset puts money in your pocket; a liability takes money out.
concept_body_en:
An asset is something you own that can put money in your pocket or grow in value over time. A liability is something you owe or something that costs you money regularly. The same physical item can be an asset for one person and a liability for another, depending on how it is used.

For example, a motorbike bought with cash and used to earn income as an ojek online driver is an asset because it helps generate money. The same motorbike bought on credit just for weekend fun is a liability because i
indonesian_example_en: Dodi buys a motorbike on credit for Rp 15,000,000 to become an ojek online driver. Every month he earns Rp 2,500,000 extra income and pays a Rp 800,000 installment. For him, the motorbike is an asset because it helps him earn more than it costs. His friend Eko buys the same motorbike on credit only for weekend rides to the mall. Eko pays the Rp 800,000 installment, fuel, and parking but earns nothing from it. For Eko, the motorbike is a liability.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Risk is the chance that reality turns out worse than you expected.
summary_id: Risiko adalah kemungkinan bahwa kenyataan berakhir lebih buruk dari yang kamu harapkan.
concept_body_en:
Risk is the possibility that an outcome will be worse than you hoped. It does not mean danger every time; it means uncertainty about results. Every financial decision carries some risk, even keeping cash under a pillow, because inflation can reduce its value.

concept_body_id:
Risiko adalah kemungkinan bahwa hasil akan lebih buruk dari yang kamu harapkan. Risiko tidak selalu berarti bahaya; risiko berarti ketidakpastian tentang hasil. Setiap keputusan finansial membawa risiko tertentu, bahkan menyimpan uang tunai di bawah bantal, karena inflasi bisa mengurangi nilainya.

Risiko menjadi lebih mudah dikelola ketika kamu menamainya dengan jelas. Tanyakan pada dirimu: apa yang bisa salah? Seberapa mungkin terjadi? Seberapa buruk dampaknya? Bisakah aku mengurangi kemungkin
indonesian_example_en: Rina lends Rp 200,000 to a classmate who often pays back late. The reward is helping a friend and possibly being helped later. The risk is that the friend never pays back on time, leaving Rina short on pulsa money. Before lending, Rina can reduce the risk by only lending what she can afford to lose or by agreeing on a clear payback date.

summary_en: Money available sooner is usually worth more than the same amount later.
summary_id: Uang yang tersedia lebih cepat biasanya lebih berharga daripada jumlah yang sama di kemudian hari.
concept_body_en:
The time value of money means that receiving the same amount of money earlier is generally better than receiving it later. The reason is opportunity cost: money in your hand today can cover needs, earn interest, or be saved for a goal. Money promised in the future may never arrive, and prices may rise while you wait.

concept_body_id:
Nilai waktu uang berarti menerima jumlah uang yang sama lebih awal umumnya lebih baik daripada menerimanya nanti. Alasannya adalah biaya kesempatan: uang di tanganmu hari ini bisa menutupi kebutuhan, menghasilkan bunga, atau ditabung untuk suatu tujuan. Uang yang dijanjikan di masa depan mungkin tidak pernah datang, dan harga bisa naik sementara kamu menunggu.

Ide ini juga bekerja sebaliknya. Jika kamu meminjam Rp 1.000.000 hari ini, kamu biasanya harus mengembalikan lebih banyak nanti karena p
indonesian_example_en: Bayu is owed Rp 500,000 by a relative. He can be paid today or in three months. If he receives it today, he can buy a phone charger he needs for online classes and still have money left for transport. If he waits three months, the charger may cost more, or he may miss classes because his phone is dead. Receiving the money today gives him more options.

summary_en: A budget is a plan that splits your income into needs, wants, and savings or debt payments.
summary_id: Anggaran adalah rencana yang membagi pemasukanmu menjadi kebutuhan, keinginan, serta tabungan atau pembayaran utang.
concept_body_en:
A budget is a written plan for how you will spend and save your money. The 50/30/20 framework is one simple starting point: about 50% for needs, 30% for wants, and 20% for savings and paying off debt. In Indonesia, you may need to adjust these numbers based on family contributions, living costs, and local prices. A student living with parents might save 30%, while someone paying full kos might only save 10%.

The real value of a budget is not perfection. It is awareness. When you know where your
concept_body_id: Anggaran adalah rencana tertulis tentang bagaimana kamu akan membelanjakan dan menabung uangmu. Kerangka 50/30/20 adalah titik awal yang sederhana: sekitar 50% untuk kebutuhan, 30% untuk keinginan, dan 20% untuk tabungan serta melunasi utang. Di Indonesia, kamu mungkin perlu menyesuaikan angka-angka ini berdasarkan kontribusi keluarga, biaya hidup, dan harga lokal. Mahasiswa yang tinggal dengan orang tua mungkin bisa menabung 30%, sementara yang membayar kos penuh mungkin hanya bisa menabung 10%
indonesian_example_en: Ani earns Rp 2,000,000 per month from a part-time job. She spends Rp 1,000,000 on needs like kos, campus meals, and pulsa. She allocates Rp 600,000 for wants like streaming subscriptions and hanging out with friends. That leaves Rp 400,000 for savings and paying back a small debt to her brother. This simple split keeps her from borrowing more and lets her build an emergency fund over time.

summary_en: Save automatically at the start of the month instead of hoping something is left at the end.
summary_id: Menabung otomatis di awal bulan, bukan berharap ada sisa di akhir bulan.
concept_body_en:
Pay yourself first means transferring money to savings before you spend on anything else. Instead of waiting to see what is left at the end of the month, you decide in advance how much to save and move it immediately when income arrives.

This works because willpower is limited. If saving is the last priority, it often disappears into small daily purchases like extra coffee, snacks, or impulse app purchases. Automating the transfer makes saving a default, not a decision. Even a small amount save

Bayar diri sendiri dulu berarti memindahkan uang ke tabungan sebelum kamu membelanjakan apa pun. Alih-alih menunggu sisa di akhir bulan, kamu memutuskan berapa banyak yang akan ditabung dan memindahkannya segera saat pendapatan datang.

Ini berhasil karena tekad kita terbatas. Jika menabung adalah prioritas terakhir, sering kali uang itu lenyap dalam pembelian kecil harian seperti kopi tambahan, camilan, atau pembelian aplikasi impulsif. Mengotomatisasi transfer membuat menabung menjadi default,
indonesian_example_en: Every month when Doni's Rp 2,000,000 part-time salary arrives, his banking app automatically moves Rp 300,000 to a separate tabungan labeled 'Future Me.' Only then does he buy pulsa, coffee, or hang out with friends. Some months he has less to spend, but his savings grow steadily because they leave his account first.

Common traps include flash sales that create fake urgency, influencer recommendations that make you feel left out, and small daily treats that seem cheap alone but add up fast. Sellers use countdown timers, limited-stock labels, and social proof to push you toward quick decisions.

Jebakan pengeluaran adalah apa pun yang menipumu agar membeli lebih dari yang direncanakan. Jebakan umum meliputi flash sale yang menciptakan urgensi palsu, rekomendasi influencer yang membuatmu merasa ketinggalan, dan camilan kecil harian yang terasa murah sendiri tapi cepat bertumpuk. Penjual menggunakan penghitung waktu mundur, label stok terbatas, dan bukti sosial untuk mendorongmu memutuskan dengan cepat.

She closes the app and saves the skincare for next month if she still wants it.

summary_en: Your emotions can push you to follow the crowd, fear losses, or chase trends without thinking.
summary_id: Emosimu bisa mendorongmu ikut-ikutan kerumunan, takut rugi, atau kejar tren tanpa berpikir.
concept_body_en:
Behavioral bias means mental shortcuts that can lead to poor financial decisions. Three common biases are FOMO, or fear of missing out, which makes you buy something just because others are buying it; loss aversion, which makes the pain of losing money feel stronger than the joy of gaining the same amount; and herd behavior, which makes you follow the crowd without doing your own research.

These biases are normal, but they can be costly. The best defense is to slow down, write down your reason
concept_body_id:
Bias perilaku artinya jalan pintas berpikir yang bisa mengarah ke keputusan finansial buruk. Tiga bias umum adalah FOMO, atau fear of missing out, yang membuatmu membeli sesuatu hanya karena orang lain juga beli; loss aversion, yang membuat rasa sakit rugi uang terasa lebih kuat daripada senangnya dapat uang dalam jumlah sama; dan herd behavior, yang membuatmu mengikuti kerumunan tanpa riset sendiri.

Bias-bias ini wajar, tapi bisa mahal. Pertahanan terbaik adalah melambat, menuliskan alasan kep
indonesian_example_en: All of Bayu's friends are buying GOTO stock with Rp 1,000,000 each because of a viral TikTok video saying the price will double. Bayu feels FOMO because he does not want to miss out. He also feels loss aversion because he is afraid of losing his Rp 1,000,000. Instead of buying immediately, he writes down his reason: 'Because TikTok said so.' He realizes this is herd behavior, not research. He decides to learn more about the company first and only invests an amount he can afford to lose.

summary_en: Guaranteed high returns with no risk do not exist; that promise is a classic scam sign.
summary_id: Imbal hasil tinggi yang dijamin tanpa risiko tidak ada; janji itu adalah tanda penipuan klasik.
concept_body_en:
If an investment promises high returns, zero risk, and pressure to recruit friends, it is almost certainly a scam. In finance, return and risk are connected. Anyone promising guaranteed profit is either lying or hiding the risk. OJK regularly warns the public about illegal investments that use these exact tricks.

Jika sebuah investasi menjanjikan imbal hasil tinggi, risiko nol, dan tekanan untuk merekrut teman, itu hampir pasti penipuan. Dalam keuangan, imbal hasil dan risiko saling terhubung. Siapa pun yang menjanjikan keuntungan pasti berbohong atau menyembunyikan risikonya. OJK secara rutin memperingatkan masyarakat tentang investasi ilegal yang menggunakan trik persis ini.

The group asks members to deposit at least Rp 1,000,000. His friend pressures him to join before the 'slots close.' Bayu remembers that OJK says guaranteed returns are impossible. He checks the OJK Waspada Investasi portal, does not find the product, and leaves the group.

OJK, Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, melisensi dan mengawasi bank, perusahaan asuransi, manajer investasi, dan banyak produk investasi. Produk yang tidak terdaftar di situs web OJK adalah ilegal dan tidak dilindungi. Jika perusahaan gagal atau lari dengan uangmu, peluang pemulihanmu sangat kecil.

Phishing is a fake message designed to steal your personal data, passwords, or OTP. summary_en: A real business earns money from customers; a pyramid scheme earns money from recruits.
summary_id: Bisnis sungguhan menghasilkan uang dari pelanggan; skema piramida menghasilkan uang dari perekrutan.

A legitimate multi-level marketing company mainly earns money by selling real products to real customers. A pyramid scheme mainly earns money by recruiting new members who pay fees or buy inventory. Pyramid schemes collapse when recruitment slows because there are not enough new people to pay the old ones.

Skema piramida utamanya menghasilkan uang dengan merekrut anggota baru yang membayar biaya atau membeli stok. title_en: Debt Traps: PayLater, Pinjol, and Credit Cards
title_id: Jebakan Utang: PayLater, Pinjol, dan Kartu Kredit
summary_en: High-interest consumer debt can grow faster than your ability to pay it back.
summary_id: Utang konsumen berbunga tinggi bisa tumbuh lebih cepat dari kemampuanmu membayarnya.
concept_body_en:
Debt is money you borrow and promise to repay later, usually with extra cost called interest. Debt becomes a trap when the interest or late fees grow faster than your income. In Indonesia, PayLater apps, online loans (pinjol), and credit cards make borrowing feel easy, but missing a payment can cause the balance to balloon.

The safest strategy is to avoid borrowing for things that lose value quickly, such as clothes or gadgets. If you already have high-interest debt, the fastest escape is usual
concept_body_id:
Utang adalah uang yang kamu pinjam dan berjanji membayarnya kembali nanti, biasanya dengan biaya tambahan yang disebut bunga. Utang menjadi jebakan ketika bunga atau denda keterlambatan tumbuh lebih cepat dari pendapatanmu. Di Indonesia, aplikasi PayLater, pinjaman online (pinjol), dan kartu kredit membuat berhutang terasa mudah, tapi ketinggalan satu pembayaran bisa membuat saldo membengkak.

Strategi teraman adalah menghindari berhutang untuk barang-barang yang cepat kehilangan nilai, seperti
indonesian_example_en: Raka uses PayLater to buy a Rp 1,200,000 hoodie. He forgets the due date and the bill grows to Rp 1,500,000 after late fees and interest. His monthly allowance is only Rp 1,500,000, so now most of it is gone before he buys food or pulsa. He should have saved for the hoodie first or skipped it, and now he must negotiate a payment plan and stop using PayLater until it is paid off.

summary_en: Some debt helps you earn more or own assets that grow in value; other debt only buys things that lose value and create monthly stress.
concept_body_en: Debt is not automatically good or bad — it depends on what the money produces. Good debt is borrowed money that is likely to increase your future income or net worth. Examples include a low-cost education loan that leads to a better job, a KUR (Kredit Usaha Rakyat) loan that starts a profitable small business, or a mortgage on a rental property that generates income. Bad debt is borrowed money spent on things that lose value quickly and do not produce income, such as gadgets, clothes, or vacatio
indonesian_example_en: Sari borrows Rp 5,000,000 for an online coding bootcamp. After finishing, she gets a junior developer job that pays Rp 7,000,000 per month. The loan was good debt because it increased her earning power. Her friend Rina uses PayLater to buy a Rp 1,200,000 hoodie. She misses the due date and the total grows to Rp 1,500,000 after fees and interest. The hoodie was bad debt because it lost value immediately and created extra cost.
sources: OJK-014: OJK Pocket Guide — Personal Financial Management PDF (https://www.ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi/Documents/Pages/Buku-Saku-Pengelolaan-Keuangan-Pribadi/Buku-Saku-Pengelolaan-Keuangan-Pribadi.pdf) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: PayLater and buy-now-pay-later plans make spending feel free, but late fees, interest, and impulse buying can turn a small purchase into a stressful debt.
concept_body_en:
Buy-now-pay-later (BNPL), often called PayLater in Indonesian apps, lets you split a purchase into small installments. This feels affordable, but it hides the full cost and encourages buying things you do not need. If you miss a due date, late fees and interest can make the item far more expensive than the original price. Many users end up with several PayLater bills at once and struggle to track them all.

Even licensed PayLater providers are required to follow OJK rules, but the product itself
indonesian_example_en: Bayu buys a Rp 900,000 gaming headset using PayLater in three installments of Rp 300,000. He forgets the second due date and is charged a Rp 150,000 late fee plus interest. The headset now costs Rp 1,150,000, and he still has to pay his phone bill and campus meals. The small installment felt safe, but one missed payment turned it into a budget problem.
sources: OJK-009: OJK SWI Cyber Patrol — Illegal Investment & Fintech Lending Crackdown (https://www.ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/siaran-pers/Pages/Siaran-Pers-Satgas-Waspada-Investasi-Gencarkan-Cyber-Patrol--Tindak-Fintech-Lending-dan-Penawaran-Investasi-illegal.aspx) [PRIMARY] | OJK-012: OJK Banking Consumer Protection (https://www.ojk.go.id/id/kanal/perbankan/edukasi-dan-perlindungan-konsumen/Pages/default.aspx)

summary_en: A credit card is a tool. It rewards disciplined users with convenience and credit history, and punishes those who only pay the minimum.
concept_body_en:
A credit card is not free money. It is a short-term loan from a bank. In Indonesia, Bank Indonesia regulates credit cards through PBI No.14/2/PBI/2012. The rules cover maximum interest rates, minimum age and income requirements, credit limits, and consumer protection. These rules exist because revolving credit can be expensive when misused.

A credit card can be good when you pay the full balance every month. You build a positive SLIK credit record, enjoy a short grace period before payment, and
indonesian_example_en: Citra uses her BCA credit card only for monthly groceries and fuel, then pays the full bill automatically from her tabungan. She never pays interest and earns small cashback. Her older brother Doni uses his credit card to buy a new phone and only pays the minimum each month. The remaining balance grows with interest, and after six months he has paid more in interest than the phone is worth.
sources: BI-010: Peraturan Bank Indonesia No.14/2/PBI/2012 tentang Penyelenggaraan Kegiatan Alat Pembayaran Dengan Menggunakan Kartu (https://www.bi.go.id/id/publikasi/peraturan/Pages/pbi_140212.aspx) [PRIMARY] | OJK-012: OJK Banking Consumer Protection (https://www.ojk.go.id/id/kanal/perbankan/edukasi-dan-perlindungan-konsumen/Pages/default.aspx)

title_id: Cara Membayar Utang dengan Bertanggung Jawab
summary_en: A clear repayment plan protects your budget, your credit record, and your peace of mind.
concept_body_en:
The first step in paying debt responsibly is to stop adding new debt. Then list every debt you have: the lender, the remaining balance, the interest rate, the minimum payment, and the due date. This simple list removes the fear of the unknown and lets you choose a strategy.

Two popular strategies are the avalanche method and the snowball method. Avalanche means paying the minimum on every debt, then putting all extra money toward the debt with the highest interest rate. This saves the most mone
indonesian_example_en: Raka has three debts: an online loan (pinjol) of Rp 2,000,000 at 36% per year, a credit card balance of Rp 5,000,000 at 24% per year, and a loan from his brother of Rp 1,000,000 at 0% interest. He pays the minimums on the credit card and brother loan, then puts all extra money toward the pinjol. Once the pinjol is gone, he attacks the credit card next. This avalanche approach saves him the most interest.
sources: OJK-014: OJK Pocket Guide — Personal Financial Management PDF (https://www.ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi/Documents/Pages/Buku-Saku-Pengelolaan-Keuangan-Pribadi/Buku-Saku-Pengelolaan-Keuangan-Pribadi.pdf) [PRIMARY] | OJK-012: OJK Banking Consumer Protection (https://www.ojk.go.id/id/kanal/perbankan/edukasi-dan-perlindungan-konsumen/Pages/default.aspx)

title_en: Emergency Fund: Prepare Before You Invest
summary_en: An emergency fund is a separate safety net that protects your long-term savings from surprise expenses.
summary_id: Dana darurat adalah jaring pengaman terpisah yang melindungi tabungan jangka panjangmu dari pengeluaran mendadak.
concept_body_en:
An emergency fund is money set aside specifically for urgent, unexpected costs such as illness, job loss, or a broken phone. A common guide is to save three to six months of regular expenses. If your income is stable and you have no dependents, three months may be enough. If your income is irregular or you support family, aim closer to six months or more.

The fund should be kept in a safe and easy-to-access place, such as a separate savings account at an LPS-insured bank, a short-term deposit,
concept_body_id:
Dana darurat adalah uang yang disisihkan khusus untuk biaya mendesak dan tak terduga seperti sakit, kehilangan pekerjaan, atau ponsel rusak. Panduan umum adalah menabung tiga hingga enam bulan pengeluaran rutin. Jika pendapatanmu stabil dan tidak ada tanggungan, tiga bulan mungkin cukup. Jika pendapatanmu tidak tetap atau kamu menanggung keluarga, targetkan mendekati enam bulan atau lebih.

Dana ini sebaiknya disimpan di tempat yang aman dan mudah diakses, seperti rekening tabungan terpisah di b
indonesian_example_en: Budi is an ojek online driver with irregular income. His monthly expenses for kos, food, and fuel total Rp 3,000,000. One day his phone breaks, costing Rp 3,000,000 to repair. Because he has kept Rp 18,000,000 in a separate tabungan as an emergency fund, he can fix the phone without borrowing from a pinjol app or selling his motorbike.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY] | GLB-004: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel (null) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal)

summary_en: Clear goals with amounts and deadlines turn wishes into achievable plans.
summary_id: Tujuan yang jelas dengan nominal dan tenggat waktu mengubah keinginan menjadi rencana yang bisa dicapai.
concept_body_en:
A financial goal is a target you set for your money. Good goals are specific, have an amount, and have a deadline. Vague goals like 'save more' rarely work because there is no way to measure progress. A better goal is 'save Rp 5,000,000 for a laptop by December.'

Goals are usually grouped by time. Short-term goals are under one year, such as buying a phone. Medium-term goals are one to five years, such as building an emergency fund or funding a course. Long-term goals are more than five years,
concept_body_id:
Tujuan keuangan adalah target yang kamu tetapkan untuk uangmu. Tujuan yang baik spesifik, punya nominal, dan punya tenggat waktu. Tujuan kabur seperti 'menabung lebih banyak' jarang berhasil karena tidak ada cara mengukur kemajuan. Tujuan yang lebih baik adalah 'menabung Rp 5.000.000 untuk laptop pada Desember.'

Tujuan biasanya dikelompokkan berdasarkan waktu. Tujuan jangka pendek adalah di bawah satu tahun, seperti membeli ponsel. Tujuan jangka menengah adalah satu hingga lima tahun, seperti m
indonesian_example_en: Fani wants a Rp 5,000,000 laptop in 10 months for college. Instead of hoping money appears, she divides the target by ten. She needs to save Rp 500,000 per month. She sets an automatic transfer of Rp 500,000 to a separate tabungan on payday. Each month she checks her progress and adjusts spending if she falls behind.
sources: GLB-008: Tiny Habits — BJ Fogg (product design reference) (null) | OJK-002: OJK National Survey on Financial Literacy & Inclusion (SNLIK) 2025 (https://ojk.go.id/id/Fungsi-Utama/Perilaku-Pelaku-Usaha-Jasa-Keuangan/SNLIK/Pages/SNLIK-2025.aspx) | OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: A financial plan puts goals, emergency savings, debt, protection, and investing into one clear order.
summary_id: Rencana keuangan menyusun tujuan, dana darurat, utang, perlindungan, dan investasi dalam satu urutan yang jelas.
concept_body_en:
A financial plan is a simple map of where your money should go. For most young Indonesians, the first steps are: cover basic needs, build a small emergency fund, pay off high-interest debt, protect yourself with health coverage such as BPJS Kesehatan or private health insurance if possible, and only then consider investing. The order matters because there is no point chasing investment returns while an emergency or high-interest debt can wipe you out.

Your plan should match your life. If you ha
concept_body_id: Rencana keuangan adalah peta sederhana soal ke mana uangmu harus pergi. Bagi kebanyakan anak muda Indonesia, langkah awalnya adalah: penuhi kebutuhan dasar, bangun dana darurat kecil, lunasi utang berbunga tinggi, lindungi diri dengan perlindungan kesehatan seperti BPJS Kesehatan atau asuransi kesehatan swasta kalau memungkinkan, dan baru setelah itu pertimbangkan investasi. Urutannya penting karena tidak ada gunanya mengejar imbal hasil investasi sementara dana darurat atau utang berbunga tingg
indonesian_example_en: Ani is 19 and earns Rp 2,500,000 per month from freelance design. She has no emergency fund and Rp 2,000,000 in PayLater debt with high interest. Her financial plan starts with covering basic needs, building a one-month emergency fund of Rp 1,500,000, then aggressively paying off the PayLater debt. Only after the debt is gone does she think about investing Rp 100,000 per month in a reksa dana.
sources: GLB-005: I Will Teach You To Be Rich — Ramit Sethi (null) | OJK-001: National Strategy on Indonesian Financial Literacy (SNLKI) 2021-2025 (https://ojk.go.id/en/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi/Pages/National-Strategy-on-Indonesian-Financial-Literacy-(SNLKI)-2021---2025.aspx) [PRIMARY] | OJK-002: OJK National Survey on Financial Literacy & Inclusion (SNLIK) 2025 (https://ojk.go.id/id/Fungsi-Utama/Perilaku-Pelaku-Usaha-Jasa-Keuangan/SNLIK/Pages/SNLIK-2025.aspx)

summary_en: Interest is the cost of borrowing money or the reward for saving it.
concept_body_en:
Interest is the extra money you pay when you borrow, or the extra money you receive when you save or lend. When you deposit money in a bank, the bank pays you interest because it can use your money to make loans. When you borrow, you pay interest because the lender gave up the use of that money.

Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount. For example, 4% annual interest on Rp 1,000,000 gives you Rp 40,000 in one year. The interest rate matters because it affects how fast debt gro
indonesian_example_en: Rina saves Rp 1,000,000 in a bank deposito that pays 4% per year. After one year, she earns Rp 40,000 in interest before tax. The bank uses her deposit and others like it to fund loans for businesses and other customers. Rina's reward is the interest, and the bank's reward is the difference between what it pays savers and what it charges borrowers.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

title_id: Bunga Majemuk: Uang yang Membuat Uang
summary_en: Compound interest means earning interest on your interest, which grows faster over time.
summary_id: Bunga majemuk artinya kamu mendapat bunga dari bunga yang sudah dihasilkan, jadi uangmu tumbuh lebih cepat seiring waktu.
concept_body_en:
Compound interest happens when you earn interest not only on the money you originally saved, but also on the interest that money has already earned. This creates a snowball effect: the longer you leave the money, the faster it grows. The two most important factors are time and the interest rate.

Starting early matters more than starting big. A small amount saved early can grow larger than a bigger amount saved later because it has more time to compound. Of course, in real life returns are not g
concept_body_id:
Bunga majemuk terjadi saat kamu mendapat bunga bukan hanya dari uang yang pertama kali disimpan, tapi juga dari bunga yang sudah dihasilkan uang itu. Ini menciptakan efek bola salju: semakin lama uang dibiarkan, semakin cepat pertumbuhannya. Dua faktor paling penting adalah waktu dan suku bunga.

Memulai lebih awal lebih berarti daripada memulai dalam jumlah besar. Tabungan kecil yang dimulai awal bisa tumbuh lebih besar dari tabungan besar yang dimulai belakangan karena punya lebih banyak waktu
indonesian_example_en: Doni saves Rp 100,000 every month starting at age 18 in an instrument that averages 6% per year. His brother starts saving the same amount at age 28. By age 40, Doni has contributed only Rp 12,000,000 more than his brother but ends up with far more because his money compounded for ten extra years. The extra decade of compounding makes the difference.
sources: GLB-004: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel (null) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY]

title_en: Bank vs Investment: Where Should Your Money Go?
title_id: Bank vs Investasi: Uangmu Harus ke Mana?
summary_en: Banks protect short-term money; investments may grow long-term money but carry risk.
summary_id: Bank melindungi uang jangka pendek; investasi bisa menumbuhkan uang jangka panjang tapi punya risiko.
concept_body_en:
A bank account is a place to keep money safe and easy to access. Savings and deposits usually pay lower, more stable interest and are protected by programs like LPS within limits. Investments, such as stocks, bonds, or reksa dana, offer the chance of higher returns but also carry the risk of losing value.

The right place depends on when you need the money. Money you need soon, such as next month's tuition or an emergency fund, belongs in a bank. Money you will not need for many years can be con
concept_body_id:
Rekening bank adalah tempat menyimpan uang yang aman dan mudah diambil. Tabungan dan deposito biasanya memberikan bunga lebih rendah dan stabil, serta dilindungi oleh program seperti LPS dalam batas tertentu. Investasi seperti saham, obligasi, atau reksa dana menawarkan peluang imbal hasil lebih tinggi tapi juga risiko nilai merosot.

Tempat yang tepat bergantung pada kapan kamu butuh uangnya. Uang yang segera dibutuhkan, seperti uang kuliah bulan depan atau dana darurat, sebaiknya disimpan di b
indonesian_example_en: Bayu has Rp 5,000,000. He needs Rp 2,000,000 next month for tuition, so he keeps it in a regular tabungan for safety. He can lock away Rp 3,000,000 for at least two years, so he considers a low-risk reksa dana. He does not put next month's tuition in stocks because the value could drop right when he needs it.
sources: GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Higher potential returns usually come with higher risk; there is no safe way to earn big quickly.
summary_id: Potensi imbal hasil yang lebih tinggi biasanya datang dengan risiko lebih besar; tidak ada cara aman untuk kaya cepat.
concept_body_en:
Return is the money you gain or lose on an investment over time. Risk is the chance that the actual return will be worse than expected. In general, investments that offer higher potential returns also carry higher risk. This is sometimes called the risk-return trade-off.

There is no free lunch in finance. If someone promises high return with little or no risk, they are likely hiding something or running a scam. Safe tools like bank deposits protect your money but usually grow slowly. Riskier to
concept_body_id:
Imbal hasil adalah uang yang kamu dapat atau rugi dari investasi seiring waktu. Risiko adalah kemungkinan imbal hasil aktual lebih buruk dari perkiraan. Secara umum, investasi dengan potensi imbal hasil lebih tinggi juga membawa risiko lebih besar. Ini sering disebut trade-off risiko dan imbal hasil.

Tidak ada makan siang gratis di dunia keuangan. Jika ada yang menjanjikan imbal hasil tinggi dengan risiko kecil atau tanpa risiko, kemungkinan mereka menyembunyikan sesuatu atau menjalankan penipu
indonesian_example_en: Rina has Rp 10,000,000 to set aside. A bank tabungan pays 2% per year with low risk; her balance is safe and easy to withdraw. A reksa dana saham has the potential for higher returns but its value can drop 10% or more in a bad month. If she needs the money in five months, the tabungan is better. If she can leave it for five years, the reksa dana saham may be worth considering because she has time to wait out short-term drops.
sources: GLB-004: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel (null) | GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY]

title_en: Diversification: Don't Put All Eggs in One Basket
title_id: Diversifikasi: Jangan Taruh Semua Telur dalam Satu Keranjang
summary_en: Spreading your money across different assets reduces the damage when one of them falls.
summary_id: Menyebarkan uang ke berbagai aset mengurangi kerugian saat salah satunya turun.
concept_body_en:
Diversification means spreading money across different investments, industries, or asset types so that one bad event does not wipe everything out. If all your money is in one stock and that company has a scandal, you could lose a lot. If your money is spread across many stocks, bonds, and cash, one problem has less impact.

Diversification does not guarantee profit or remove all risk. Markets can still fall broadly. But it reduces the risk that a single mistake or bad news event will destroy you
concept_body_id:
Diversifikasi artinya menyebarkan uang ke berbagai investasi, industri, atau jenis aset agar satu peristiwa buruk tidak menghabiskan semuanya. Jika semua uangmu di satu saham dan perusahaan itu terlibat skandal, kamu bisa rugi besar. Jika uangmu tersebar di banyak saham, obligasi, dan tunai, satu masalah punya dampak lebih kecil.

Diversifikasi tidak menjamin untung atau menghilangkan semua risiko. Pasar masih bisa turun secara luas. Tapi diversifikasi mengurangi risiko bahwa satu kesalahan atau
indonesian_example_en: Warung A only sells mie ayam for Rp 15,000. When chicken prices spike, sales collapse because customers cannot afford the new price of Rp 20,000. Warung B sells mie ayam for Rp 15,000, es teh for Rp 5,000, and nasi goreng for Rp 18,000. If one item becomes expensive, customers can still buy the others. Warung B is more diversified because it is not dependent on one product.
sources: IDX-001: IDX Academy — Investor Education Portal (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investasi) [PRIMARY] | GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal)

summary_en: A reksa dana pools money from many people and invests it through a licensed manager.
summary_id: Reksa dana mengumpulkan uang dari banyak orang dan menginvestasikannya melalui manajer berizin.
concept_body_en:
A reksa dana, or mutual fund, is a pool of money collected from many investors and managed by a licensed investment manager. When you buy units of a reksa dana, you own a small share of the whole pool. The fund invests in a mix of assets according to its rules.

The three main types are money market funds, which are the safest and most liquid; fixed income funds, which invest in bonds and offer moderate risk; and equity funds, which invest in stocks and carry higher risk with higher potential re
concept_body_id:
Reksa dana, atau mutual fund, adalah kumpulan uang dari banyak investor yang dikelola oleh manajer investasi berizin. Saat kamu membeli unit reksa dana, kamu memiliki bagian kecil dari keseluruhan dana. Dana itu diinvestasikan dalam campuran aset sesuai aturan yang berlaku.

Tiga jenis utama adalah reksa dana pasar uang, yang paling aman dan paling likuid; reksa dana pendapatan tetap, yang berinvestasi di obligasi dan menawarkan risiko sedang; serta reksa dana saham, yang berinvestasi di saham d
indonesian_example_en: Ani wants to start investing but does not know how to pick individual stocks. She opens an account with an OJK-registered investment manager and buys Rp 500,000 of an equity reksa dana. Her money is pooled with thousands of other investors and spread across many companies. She owns a tiny slice of each company in the fund, giving her instant diversification without choosing stocks herself.
sources: GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: A stock is a small piece of ownership in a company.
summary_id: Saham itu bagian kecil dari kepemilikan sebuah perusahaan.
concept_body_en:
A stock, or saham, is a share of ownership in a company. When you buy a stock, you become one of the owners of that company, even if your share is tiny. As an owner, you may benefit if the company grows and becomes more valuable, but you may also lose money if the company performs poorly.

Stock prices change because buyers and sellers disagree on what a company is worth. If more people want to buy than sell, the price tends to rise. If more people want to sell than buy, the price tends to fall.
concept_body_id:
Saham, atau stock, adalah bagian kepemilikan dalam sebuah perusahaan. Saat kamu membeli saham, kamu jadi salah satu pemilik perusahaan itu, meski bagiannya kecil. Sebagai pemilik, kamu bisa untung kalau perusahaan berkembang dan makin berharga, tapi juga bisa rugi kalau performanya jelek.

Harga saham berubah karena pembeli dan penjual punya pendapat berbeda soal nilai perusahaan. Kalau yang mau beli lebih banyak dari yang mau jual, harga cenderung naik. Kalau yang mau jual lebih banyak, harga c
indonesian_example_en: Bayu buys one lot of BBCA, which is Bank Central Asia stock listed on IDX, at Rp 8,550 per share. One lot equals 100 shares, so he spends Rp 855,000 plus fees. He now owns a very small piece of Bank Central Asia. If the bank earns more profit and investors believe in its future, more people may want to buy the stock and the price may rise. If the bank has problems, the price may fall.
sources: GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | IDX-001: IDX Academy — Investor Education Portal (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investasi) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: IDX has clear rules: stocks trade in lots of 100 shares, and investor protection programs exist for listed securities.
summary_id: IDX punya aturan jelas: saham diperdagangkan dalam lot 100 lembar, dan ada program perlindungan investor untuk efek yang tercatat.
concept_body_en:
IDX stands for Bursa Efek Indonesia, the Indonesia Stock Exchange. It is the regulated marketplace where stocks and other securities trade. On IDX, stocks are bought and sold in lots, and one standard lot is 100 shares. This means you cannot buy just one share of a listed company; you must buy at least one lot.

concept_body_id:
IDX adalah singkatan dari Bursa Efek Indonesia, tempat saham dan efek lain diperdagangkan secara teregulasi. Di IDX, saham dibeli dan dijual dalam satuan lot, dan satu lot standar adalah 100 lembar saham. Artinya, kamu tidak bisa beli hanya satu lembar saham perusahaan tercatat; minimal harus beli satu lot.

Perdagangan IDX berlangsung di hari kerja, biasanya Senin sampai Jumat. Ada juga mekanisme perlindungan investor, seperti SIPF (Securities Investor Protection Fund), yang memberikan perlindu
indonesian_example_en: Doni wants to buy shares of TLKM, Telkom Indonesia. He has Rp 1,000,000 and the stock price is Rp 3,800 per share. He thinks he can buy about 263 shares, but on IDX he must buy in lots of 100. He can buy either 100 shares for Rp 380,000 or 200 shares for Rp 760,000. He chooses one lot of 100 shares and keeps the rest in his tabungan.
sources: IDX-002: IDX Glossary of Capital Markets Terms (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pasar_modal) | IDX-005: IDX — Beginner Investment Guide (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investasi) | IDX-007: IDX Investor Protection — SIPF (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investor_protection) | GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | IDX-001: IDX Academy — Investor Education Portal (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investasi) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: A stock summary shows the price range, closing price, trading volume, and total company value.
summary_id: Ringkasan saham menunjukkan rentang harga, harga penutupan, volume perdagangan, dan nilai total perusahaan.
concept_body_en:
A stock page shows numbers that describe how a stock traded during the day. Open is the price at the start of trading. High is the highest price reached. Low is the lowest price reached. Close is the last price before the market closed. Volume is how many shares changed hands. Market capitalization, or market cap, is the total value of all the company's shares multiplied by the current price.

These numbers describe activity, not quality. A high volume means many people traded that day. A high p
concept_body_id:
Halaman saham menampilkan angka-angka yang menggambarkan bagaimana saham bertransaksi dalam sehari. Open adalah harga di awal perdagangan. High adalah harga tertinggi yang tercapai. Low adalah harga terendah yang tercapai. Close adalah harga terakhir sebelum pasar tutup. Volume adalah jumlah saham yang berpindah tangan. Market capitalization, atau kapitalisasi pasar, adalah nilai total seluruh saham perusahaan dikalikan harga saat ini.

Angka-angka ini menggambarkan aktivitas, bukan kualitas. Vo
indonesian_example_en: Bayu looks at a simplified BBCA stock card from IDX. It shows open Rp 8,450, high Rp 8,620, low Rp 8,400, close Rp 8,550, and volume 45 million shares. Bayu sees that the price moved between Rp 8,400 and Rp 8,620 during the day and ended at Rp 8,550. The volume of 45 million tells him many people traded BBCA shares that day, but it does not tell him whether the price will rise tomorrow.

summary_en: A portfolio is the whole combination of your holdings, and its mix should match your goals.
summary_id: Portofolio adalah gabungan seluruh kepemilikanmu, dan komposisinya harus sesuai dengan tujuanmu.
concept_body_en:
A portfolio is the combination of all the financial assets you own, such as cash, savings, reksa dana, and stocks. Portfolio thinking means looking at the whole picture instead of judging each item alone. A single stock may be risky, but a small amount of stock inside a larger portfolio can be reasonable.

The right mix depends on your goals and time horizon. Money you need soon should be in safer, easy-to-access places. Money you will not need for years can include more growth assets. As your g
concept_body_id:
Portofolio adalah gabungan dari semua aset keuangan yang kamu miliki, seperti tunai, tabungan, reksa dana, dan saham. Berpikir portofolio berarti melihat gambaran besar, bukan menilai satu-satu aset sendiri. Satu saham mungkin berisiko, tapi porsi kecil saham dalam portofolio yang lebih besar bisa masuk akal.

Komposisi yang tepat tergantung pada tujuan dan jangka waktumu. Uang yang segera dibutuhkan sebaiknya disimpan di tempat yang aman dan mudah diakses. Uang yang tidak dibutuhkan bertahun-ta
indonesian_example_en: Rina has Rp 10,000,000 in total. She keeps Rp 3,000,000 in a bank tabungan for emergencies, Rp 4,000,000 in a money market reksa dana for a laptop she wants in one year, and Rp 3,000,000 in one stock she likes. This is her portfolio. The missing piece is diversification in the stock part. If her goal were building a pension fund or starting a business in 20–30 years, she might keep less in cash and spread the stock money across more companies or a reksa dana saham.
sources: IDX-001: IDX Academy — Investor Education Portal (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investasi) [PRIMARY] | GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal)

summary_en: Investment gains may be taxed, so the return you keep can be lower than the headline number.
summary_id: Keuntungan investasi bisa kena pajak, jadi imbal hasil yang kamu bawa pulang bisa lebih rendah dari angka yang tertera.
concept_body_en:
When you earn money from investments, the government may take a portion as tax. In Indonesia, different types of return can be taxed differently. For example, interest from deposits and dividends from stocks may both be subject to tax. The amount you actually keep after tax is called your net return, while the amount before tax is called your gross return.

Tax rules can change, and the details depend on your situation and the type of account. The key lesson is to compare investments using net r
concept_body_id:
Saat kamu menghasilkan uang dari investasi, pemerintah bisa mengambil sebagian sebagai pajak. Di Indonesia, jenis imbal hasil yang berbeda bisa kena pajak berbeda. Misalnya, bunga deposito dan dividen saham keduanya bisa kena pajak. Jumlah yang benar-benar kamu simpan setelah pajak disebut imbal hasil bersih, sedangkan jumlah sebelum pajak disebut imbal hasil kotor.

Aturan pajak bisa berubah, dan detailnya tergantung situasimu dan jenis rekeningnya. Pelajarannya, bandingkan investasi menggunaka
indonesian_example_en: Doni earns Rp 500,000 in interest from a deposito and Rp 1,000,000 from a stock dividend during the year. His bank statement shows the gross amounts, but after tax he keeps less. When Doni compares two investments, he should look at the net amount he will actually receive, not just the headline rate advertised by the product.
sources: OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY] | GLB-005: I Will Teach You To Be Rich — Ramit Sethi (null) | OJK-001: National Strategy on Indonesian Financial Literacy (SNLKI) 2021-2025 (https://ojk.go.id/en/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi/Pages/National-Strategy-on-Indonesian-Financial-Literacy-(SNLKI)-2021---2025.aspx)

summary_en: Big-picture signals like BI Rate, inflation, and exchange rates affect prices, interest, and your purchasing power.
summary_id: Sinyal besar seperti BI Rate, inflasi, dan nilai tukar memengaruhi harga, bunga, dan daya belimu.
concept_body_en:
Macro indicators are large-scale signals that describe the health of the economy. Three important ones in Indonesia are the BI Rate, which is the central bank's benchmark interest rate; inflation, which measures how fast prices rise; and the exchange rate, which shows how much rupiah is needed to buy one US dollar (dolar AS) or other currency.

These indicators affect your money indirectly. When BI raises the BI Rate, bank deposit interest may rise, but borrowing becomes more expensive and stock
concept_body_id:
Indikator makro adalah sinyal skala besar yang menggambarkan kesehatan ekonomi. Tiga yang penting di Indonesia adalah BI Rate, yaitu suku bunga acuan Bank Indonesia; inflasi, yang mengukur seberapa cepat harga naik; dan nilai tukar, yang menunjukkan berapa rupiah dibutuhkan untuk membeli satu dolar AS atau mata uang lain.

Indikator ini memengaruhi uangmu secara tidak langsung. Saat BI menaikkan BI Rate, bunga deposito bank bisa naik, tapi meminjam jadi lebih mahal dan harga saham bisa lebih vol
indonesian_example_en: When Bank Indonesia raises the BI Rate, the interest on Doni's Rp 10,000,000 deposito might increase from 3% to 4%. At the same time, his friend who wants to buy a new laptop imported from abroad for Rp 12,000,000 notices the price goes up because the rupiah weakened against the US dollar (dolar AS). Doni benefits slightly from higher deposit interest, but his friend pays more for the same gadget.
sources: BI-002: Bank Indonesia — BI Rate (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suku_bunga) [PRIMARY] | GLB-007: A Random Walk Down Wall Street — Malkiel (null) | OJK-001: National Strategy on Indonesian Financial Literacy (SNLKI) 2021-2025 (https://ojk.go.id/en/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi/Pages/National-Strategy-on-Indonesian-Financial-Literacy-(SNLKI)-2021---2025.aspx)

summary_en: Cryptocurrency is a digital asset that runs on a shared computer network called blockchain. Bitcoin and Ethereum are the best known, but none of them are official money in Indonesia.
concept_body_en: Cryptocurrency is digital money that exists only as records on a network called blockchain. A blockchain is a public ledger shared across thousands of computers around the world. Because many computers keep copies, it is very hard for one person to change the records alone. Bitcoin, created in 2009, was the first cryptocurrency. People often compare it to "digital gold" because its supply is limited and its price is driven by demand. Ethereum, launched in 2015, added smart contracts — small prog
indonesian_example_en: Rina sees Bitcoin priced at around Rp 700,000,000 per BTC on the news. She learns that one Bitcoin can be divided into very small units, so someone with Rp 500,000 can still buy a tiny fraction. She also learns that Bitcoin is not a company share, not a bank deposit, and not insured by LPS. Its price can move 10% or more in a single day. Rina decides to first learn how blockchain works before putting any money in.
sources: BAPPEBTI-001: Bappebti — Cek Legalitas Pelaku Usaha Perdagangan Berjangka Komoditi (https://ceklegalitas.bappebti.go.id/) [PRIMARY]

title_en: Crypto Risks and Scams in Indonesia
title_id: Risiko dan Penipuan Kripto di Indonesia
summary_en: Crypto prices can swing wildly, and scammers use fake tokens, rug pulls, and celebrity endorsements to steal money from young Indonesians.
concept_body_en:
The first risk of crypto is volatility. It is normal for a cryptocurrency to rise or fall 20% in a single day. That means someone who invests Rp 5,000,000 can see it become Rp 4,000,000 — or Rp 6,000,000 — within 24 hours. This is not a bug; it is how the market works. For someone with no emergency fund or stable income, this volatility can cause panic and poor decisions.

The second risk is scams. A *rug pull* happens when developers create a new coin, attract buyers, then disappear with the mo
indonesian_example_en: Bayu joins a Telegram group where admins promise "MoonCoin" will rise 10 times in a week. They show screenshots of profits and say the offer is only for the first 100 people. Bayu transfers Rp 2,000,000 to a personal account. Three days later, the group is deleted, the website is gone, and the price collapses from Rp 1,000 to Rp 10. Bayu loses almost everything.
sources: BAPPEBTI-001: Bappebti — Cek Legalitas Pelaku Usaha Perdagangan Berjangka Komoditi (https://ceklegalitas.bappebti.go.id/) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: If you decide to buy crypto, use a Bappebti-registered exchange, avoid P2P strangers, protect your wallet, and remember that taxes may apply.
concept_body_en:
The safest way to buy crypto in Indonesia is through a Bappebti-registered exchange. These platforms must follow know-your-customer (KYC) rules, keep records, and separate customer assets from company funds. Well-known Indonesian platforms that have stated they are Bappebti-registered include Tokocrypto, Indodax, Pintu, and Reku, but you should always check the latest list on the Bappebti website before depositing money.

Avoid peer-to-peer (P2P) deals with strangers on WhatsApp, Telegram, or In
indonesian_example_en: Dina wants to learn about crypto with Rp 1,000,000. She opens an account on a Bappebti-registered exchange, uploads her KTP for KYC, and deposits from her BCA savings account. She buys a small fraction of Bitcoin and records the date and price. She does not answer WhatsApp messages offering a "cheaper rate" and does not keep all her crypto on the exchange long-term.
sources: BAPPEBTI-001: Bappebti — Cek Legalitas Pelaku Usaha Perdagangan Berjangka Komoditi (https://ceklegalitas.bappebti.go.id/) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Buying crypto to flip it quickly is mostly speculation, not investing. Investing builds wealth through productive assets; gambling is entertainment that usually loses money.
concept_body_en:
Investing means buying something that is expected to produce income or grow because of real economic activity. For example, a reksa dana owns stocks and bonds that earn profits and interest. A deposito earns interest because the bank lends the money to businesses and homeowners. Over years, these productive assets can build wealth slowly.

Speculation means buying something mainly because you hope the price will rise quickly. Buying a new crypto token because you expect it to "moon" next week is
indonesian_example_en: Andi has Rp 5,000,000. Option A is a reksa dana campuran that invests in Indonesian companies and government bonds. Option B is a trending crypto coin he saw on TikTok, hoping it doubles in a week. Option C is an online gambling site. Andi classifies A as investing because it owns productive assets, B as speculation because it depends on price timing, and C as gambling because the odds favor the house. He chooses A because he is still building his emergency fund and does not understand B well en
sources: BAPPEBTI-001: Bappebti — Cek Legalitas Pelaku Usaha Perdagangan Berjangka Komoditi (https://ceklegalitas.bappebti.go.id/) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Kenapa kerugian terasa lebih sakit dari keuntungan, dan bagaimana FOMO membuat kita berinvestasi tanpa rencana.
concept_body_en: Aversi rugi (loss aversion) berarti rasa sakit dari kehilangan uang biasanya lebih kuat dua kali lipat dari rasa senang mendapatkan keuntungan. FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out) mendorong kita membeli aset hanya karena semua orang membicarakannya. Kombinasi keduanya sering membuat investor muda Indonesia jual saham bagus saat turun dan beli saham hype saat naik. Solusinya: buat aturan investasi sebelum emosi muncul.
indonesian_example_en: Rina membeli saham BBRI seharga Rp 4.200. Beberapa minggu kemudian harganya turun ke Rp 3.900. Perasaannya seperti "rugi banyak", padahal baru turun 7%. Di saat yang sama, teman-temannya ramai membeli saham teknologi yang baru viral di media sosial. Rina khawatir ketinggalan (FOMO), lalu menjual BBRI dan membeli saham tersebut tanpa riset. Seminggu kemudian saham teknologi itu turun 20%, sementara BBRI kembali naik. Rina belajar bahwa emosi bisa lebih mahal dari biaya transaksi.
sources: OJK-001: National Strategy on Indonesian Financial Literacy (SNLKI) 2021-2025 (https://ojk.go.id/en/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi/Pages/National-Strategy-on-Indonesian-Financial-Literacy-(SNLKI)-2021---2025.aspx) [PRIMARY] | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal)

summary_en: Beda orang, beda toleransi risiko. Jangan memaksakan strategi orang lain ke diri sendiri.
concept_body_en: Toleransi risiko adalah seberapa besar fluktuasi harga yang bisa kamu terima tanpa panik. Faktor-faktornya antara lain umur, penghasilan stabil, tujuan keuangan, dan horizon waktu. Overconfidence, atau terlalu percaya diri, sering membuat investor muda overtrading dan meremehkan risiko. Pilih instrumen yang sesuai dengan profilmu, bukan dengan gaya hidup influencer.
indonesian_example_en: Siti, mahasiswa semester 2 dengan uang saku Rp 1.500.000 per bulan, punya horizon investasi 10 tahun ke depan. Ia bisa mempertimbangkan portofolio agak agresif dengan campuran saham dan reksa dana. Pak Tono, pensiunan yang bergantung pada tabungan, lebih baik memilih instrumen stabil seperti deposito dan obligasi pemerintah. Jika Siti meniru portofolio konservatif Pak Tono, ia kehilangan potensi pertumbuhan jangka panjang. Jika Pak Tono meniru strategi agresif Siti, ia bisa stres saat pasar turu
sources: BI-002: Bank Indonesia — BI Rate (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suku_bunga) | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Volatilitas adalah naik turun harga normal; yang penting adalah mengendalikan reaksi emosional.
concept_body_en: Volatilitas mengukur seberapa besar harga aset berfluktuasi dalam periode tertentu. Saham seperti BBCA atau GOTO bisa naik turun beberapa persen dalam seminggu. Volatilitas itu normal, terutama di pasar saham. Risiko sesungguhnya bagi investor jangka panjang sering kali bukan volatilitas, melainkan reaksi emosional yang membuat kita jual di bawah harga wajar atau beli di puncak euforia.
indonesian_example_en: Dimas membeli saham BBCA di harga Rp 8.500. Dalam seminggu, harganya turun ke Rp 8.200 dan naik lagi ke Rp 8.700. Jika Dimas panik setiap kali cek aplikasi dan menjual saat turun, ia bisa merugi meskipun fundamental perusahaan tidak berubah. Sebaliknya, investor yang memiliki rencana dan batasan "cek harga seminggu sekali" lebih jarang membuat keputusan emosional.
sources: IDX-007: IDX Investor Protection — SIPF (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Investor_protection) [PRIMARY] | BI-002: Bank Indonesia — BI Rate (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suku_bunga)

summary_en: Money is a tool that makes trade, saving, and planning possible.
summary_id: Uang adalah alat yang membuat perdagangan, menabung, dan perencanaan jadi mungkin.
concept_body_en: Money is anything people commonly accept as payment for goods and services. In daily life, money plays three roles. First, it is a medium of exchange: instead of swapping your mie ayam for a phone charger directly, you use rupiah. Second, it is a store of value: money lets you save today and spend tomorrow. Third, it is a unit of account: it gives everything a price tag so you can compare values quickly.
concept_body_id: Uang adalah apa saja yang umum diterima orang sebagai pembayaran barang dan jasa. Dalam kehidupan sehari-hari, uang punya tiga peran. Pertama, sebagai alat tukar: alih-alih menukar mie ayammu langsung dengan charger ponsel, kamu pakai rupiah. Kedua, sebagai penyimpan nilai: uang memungkinkanmu menabung hari ini dan berbelanja besok. Ketiga, sebagai satuan hitung: uang memberi harga pada semua barang sehingga kamu bisa membandingkan nilai dengan cepat.
indonesian_example_en: Budi wants to buy a Rp 15.000 notebook. He does not need to trade his lunch for it; he hands over a Rp 20.000 note and receives Rp 5.000 back. The seller accepts rupiah because everyone agrees it has value. That agreement is what makes money work.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Inflation means the same amount of money buys less over time.
summary_id: Inflasi berarti jumlah uang yang sama bisa membeli lebih sedikit seiring waktu.
concept_body_en: Inflation is the slow rise in prices across an economy. When inflation is 5%, a Rp 10.000 bowl of mie ayam may cost Rp 10.500 next year. Your money still looks the same, but its purchasing power shrinks. Inflation is usually caused by too much money chasing too few goods, rising production costs, or currency weakness.
concept_body_id: Inflasi adalah kenaikan harga perlahan di seluruh ekonomi. Ketika inflasi 5%, semangkuk mie ayam Rp 10.000 bisa jadi Rp 10.500 tahun depan. Uangmu masih terlihat sama, tapi daya belinya mengecil. Inflasi biasanya disebabkan oleh terlalu banyak uang mengejar barang yang terlalu sedikit, biaya produksi naik, atau nilai tukar mata uang melemah.
indonesian_example_en: Last year, Rina could buy a large boba tea for Rp 25.000. This year the same drink costs Rp 28.000. Her Rp 25.000 no longer buys the drink. That is inflation eating her money's value.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Interest is the price of using money over time — either what you earn or what you pay.
summary_id: Bunga adalah harga menggunakan uang dari waktu ke waktu — baik yang kamu dapatkan maupun yang kamu bayar.
concept_body_en: Interest has two sides. When you save, a bank pays you interest for letting them use your money. When you borrow, you pay interest for using someone else's money. Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount. Compound interest is calculated on the original amount plus interest that has already been added, so growth accelerates over time.
concept_body_id: Bunga punya dua sisi. Saat menabung, bank membayar kamu bunga karena meminjam uangmu. Saat berhutang, kamu membayar bunga karena memakai uang orang lain. Bunga sederhana dihitung hanya dari jumlah pokok. Bunga majemuk dihitung dari pokok ditambah bunga yang sudah ditambahkan sebelumnya, sehingga pertumbuhannya semakin cepat dari waktu ke waktu.
indonesian_example_en: Andi saves Rp 1.000.000 in a deposit that pays 5% simple interest per year. After one year he has Rp 1.050.000. If it were 5% compound interest, the next year he would earn 5% on Rp 1.050.000, not just the original Rp 1.000.000.
sources: GLB-004: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel (null) | BI-002: Bank Indonesia — BI Rate (https://id.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suku_bunga) | OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY] | OJK-004: OJK Capital Markets Channel (https://ojk.go.id/id/kanal/pasar-modal)

summary_en: Income is money coming in. Wealth is money kept and grown.
summary_id: Pendapatan adalah uang yang masuk. Kekayaan adalah uang yang tersisa dan tumbuh.
concept_body_en: Income is what you earn from a salary, allowance, freelance work, or business. Wealth is what you own minus what you owe. A person can have a high income but low wealth if they spend everything. A person can have modest income but growing wealth if they save and invest consistently.
concept_body_id: Pendapatan adalah apa yang kamu dapatkan dari gaji, uang saku, kerja lepas, atau bisnis. Kekayaan adalah apa yang kamu miliki dikurangi apa yang kamu hutang. Seseorang bisa pendapatannya tinggi tapi kekayaannya rendah jika menghabiskan semuanya. Seseorang bisa pendapatannya sederhana tapi kekayaannya tumbuh jika rajin menabung dan berinvestasi.
indonesian_example_en: Dina earns Rp 8.000.000 per month but spends Rp 8.000.000 on rent, food, and shopping. Her income is high but her wealth is flat. Sari earns Rp 4.000.000 but saves Rp 800.000 every month. Over time, Sari's wealth grows even though her income is lower.
sources: GLB-004: The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel (null) | OJK-002: OJK National Survey on Financial Literacy & Inclusion (SNLIK) 2025 (https://ojk.go.id/id/Fungsi-Utama/Perilaku-Pelaku-Usaha-Jasa-Keuangan/SNLIK/Pages/SNLIK-2025.aspx) | OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Assets put money in your pocket. Liabilities take money out.
summary_id: Aset memasukkan uang ke kantongmu. Liabilitas mengeluarkan uang dari kantongmu.
concept_body_en: An asset is something that owns or produces value: savings, investments, a productive skill, or even a motorbike that lets you earn deliveries. A liability is something that costs you money: debt, a luxury item bought on credit, or a subscription you do not use. The same item can be either depending on how you use it.
concept_body_id: Aset adalah sesuatu yang memiliki atau menghasilkan nilai: tabungan, investasi, keterampilan produktif, atau bahkan motor yang membantumu mencari nafkah. Liabilitas adalah sesuatu yang menghabiskan uangmu: utang, barang mewah yang dibeli kredit, atau langganan yang tidak kamu pakai. Barang yang sama bisa jadi aset atau liabilitas tergantung cara kamu menggunakannya.
indonesian_example_en: A laptop bought to play games and watch Netflix is mostly a liability because it keeps costing electricity and internet. The same laptop bought to do freelance design work is an asset because it helps earn money.
sources: GLB-006: Rich Dad Poor Dad — Kiyosaki (asset/liability concept ONLY) (null) | OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Risk is the chance that something bad happens to your money.
summary_id: Risiko adalah kemungkinan sesuatu yang buruk terjadi pada uangmu.
concept_body_en: Risk is the possibility of losing money or earning less than expected. Every financial choice has risk. Keeping cash under a mattress risks theft and inflation. Putting money in a deposit risks low returns. Investing in stocks risks price drops. There is no such thing as a risk-free choice; there are only different kinds of risk.
concept_body_id: Risiko adalah kemungkinan kehilangan uang atau mendapatkan return lebih rendah dari yang diharapkan. Setiap pilihan finansial punya risiko. Menyimpan uang tunai di bawah kasur berisiko dicuri dan tergerus inflasi. Menaruh uang di deposito berisiko return rendah. Berinvestasi di saham berisiko harga turun. Tidak ada pilihan yang bebas risiko; yang ada hanya risiko yang berbeda jenis.
indonesian_example_en: Bayu has Rp 5.000.000. Option A: keep it at home. Risk: stolen or eaten by inflation. Option B: put it in a deposit. Risk: low return may not beat inflation. Option C: buy a stock. Risk: price may fall. Every option has a different risk.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Return is the gain or loss you get from an investment or saving.
summary_id: Return adalah keuntungan atau kerugian yang kamu dapat dari tabungan atau investasi.
concept_body_en: Return is the money you make or lose on your money. If you put Rp 1.000.000 into something and later it is worth Rp 1.100.000, your return is Rp 100.000 or 10%. Return can come from interest, dividends, price increases, or business profits. Higher potential return usually comes with higher risk.
concept_body_id: Return adalah uang yang kamu hasilkan atau hilangkan dari uangmu. Jika kamu menaruh Rp 1.000.000 ke sesuatu dan kemudian nilainya Rp 1.100.000, returnmu Rp 100.000 atau 10%. Return bisa berasal dari bunga, dividen, kenaikan harga, atau keuntungan bisnis. Potensi return yang lebih tinggi biasanya datang dengan risiko yang lebih tinggi.
indonesian_example_en: Citra buys a government bond for Rp 1.000.000. After a year she receives Rp 60.000 in interest and still owns the bond. Her return is Rp 60.000, or 6%. She did not need to trade anything; the return came from lending her money to the government.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Saving protects money now. Investing grows money for later.
summary_id: Menabung melindungi uang sekarang. Berinvestasi menumbuhkan uang untuk nanti.
concept_body_en: Saving is putting money somewhere safe so you can use it soon. Investing is putting money into something that may grow in value over a longer time. Saving is for emergencies and short-term goals. Investing is for goals years away, like education, a business, or retirement. You need both.
concept_body_id: Menabung adalah menyimpan uang di tempat aman agar bisa segera dipakai. Berinvestasi adalah menaruh uang ke sesuatu yang nilainya bisa tumbuh dalam jangka lebih panjang. Menabung untuk dana darurat dan tujuan jangka pendek. Berinvestasi untuk tujuan bertahun-tahun, seperti pendidikan, bisnis, atau pensiun. Kamu butuh keduanya.
indonesian_example_en: Eko has Rp 10.000.000. He keeps Rp 3.000.000 in a savings account for emergencies and invests Rp 7.000.000 in a mix of bonds and stocks for his future. The savings protect him today; the investments work for him tomorrow.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: An emergency fund is money kept safe for unexpected problems.
summary_id: Dana darurat adalah uang yang disimpan aman untuk masalah tak terduga.
concept_body_en: An emergency fund is cash you can access quickly when life surprises you: a broken phone, a medical bill, a lost job, or a family need. A common target is 3–6 months of essential expenses, but even Rp 1.000.000 is better than nothing. The fund should be safe, easy to reach, and separate from daily spending money.
concept_body_id: Dana darurat adalah uang tunai yang bisa diakses cepat ketika hidup memberi kejutan: ponsel rusak, tagihan medis, kehilangan pekerjaan, atau kebutuhan keluarga. Target umum adalah 3–6 bulan pengeluaran penting, tapi bahkan Rp 1.000.000 lebih baik daripada tidak ada. Dana ini harus aman, mudah diambil, dan terpisah dari uang belanja harian.
indonesian_example_en: Fani's motorbike breaks down and needs Rp 1.500.000 for repairs. Because she has an emergency fund, she pays without borrowing. Without it, she might use a pay-later app and pay extra fees and interest.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Needs are essentials. Wants are nice-to-haves.
summary_id: Kebutuhan adalah hal esensial. Keinginan adalah hal yang menyenangkan tapi bisa ditunda.
concept_body_en: A need is something you must have to live and function: food, shelter, basic clothes, transport to school or work. A want is something you would like but can live without: the latest phone, designer shoes, premium streaming, or extra boba. The line is personal, but being honest about the difference is the first step to budgeting.
concept_body_id: Kebutuhan adalah sesuatu yang harus kamu miliki untuk hidup dan berfungsi: makanan, tempat tinggal, pakaian dasar, transportasi ke sekolah atau kerja. Keinginan adalah sesuatu yang kamu sukai tapi bisa hidup tanpanya: ponsel terbaru, sepatu branded, streaming premium, atau boba tambahan. Garisnya bersifat pribadi, tapi jujur tentang perbedaannya adalah langkah pertama membuat anggaran.
indonesian_example_en: Hana has Rp 100.000 for the day. A Rp 20.000 lunch is a need. A Rp 45.000 frappuccino is a want. If she buys the frappuccino, she has less for transport home. Seeing the trade-off helps her decide.
sources: GLB-005: I Will Teach You To Be Rich — Ramit Sethi (null) | OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: Debt is money you owe and must pay back, usually with extra cost.
summary_id: Utang adalah uang yang kamu pinjam dan harus dikembalikan, biasanya dengan biaya tambahan.
concept_body_en: Debt happens when you borrow money and promise to repay it later. The lender usually charges interest or fees for the loan. Some debt can be useful, like a student loan that increases your earning power. Some debt is dangerous, like high-interest pay-later spending for things that lose value quickly. The key questions are: what is the interest rate, can you afford the payments, and will the debt help you earn more or just consume?
concept_body_id: Utang terjadi ketika kamu meminjam uang dan berjanji mengembalikannya nanti. Pemberi pinjaman biasanya mengenakan bunga atau biaya untuk pinjamannya. Beberapa utang bisa berguna, seperti pinjaman pendidikan yang meningkatkan daya jual kerjamu. Beberapa utang berbahaya, seperti pay-later untuk barang yang cepat turun nilainya. Pertanyaan kuncinya: berapa suku bunganya, bisakah kamu membayar cicilannya, dan apakah utang itu membantumu menghasilkan lebih banyak atau hanya untuk konsumsi?
indonesian_example_en: Irfan borrows Rp 2.000.000 from a pay-later app to buy new sneakers. The interest is 3% per month. If he only pays the minimum, the debt can grow to Rp 2.500.000 or more. The sneakers are now worth less than the debt.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]

summary_en: If it sounds too good to be true, it usually is.
summary_id: Jika terdengar terlalu bagus untuk jadi kenyataan, biasanya memang begitu.
concept_body_en: Scams often promise guaranteed high returns with little or no risk, pressure you to decide quickly, ask you to recruit friends, or pretend to be from a government agency or famous company. A real investment cannot promise fixed high returns because markets move. A real regulator will never ask for your password or OTP.
concept_body_id: Penipuan sering menjanjikan return tinggi terjamin dengan risiko kecil atau nol, menekanmu untuk cepat memutuskan, memintamu mengajak teman, atau berpura-pura dari lembaga pemerintah atau perusahaan terkenal. Investasi nyata tidak bisa menjanjikan return tetap tinggi karena pasar bergerak. Regulator nyata tidak akan pernah meminta password atau OTP-mu.
indonesian_example_en: An Instagram account promises 15% profit every month, guaranteed. They show screenshots of other people's gains and say "limited slots." They ask you to transfer money to a personal account. Every signal — guaranteed return, urgency, fake social proof, personal account — is a red flag.
sources: OJK-003: OJK Publications Portal (https://ojk.go.id/id/berita-dan-kegiatan/publikasi) [PRIMARY]
